LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a `.SRCINFO` metadata file for the `rusticlone-bin` Arch Linux package. It contains standard package metadata: package name, description, version (2.0.1), release (1), URL, architectures (x86_64, aarch64, armv7h), license (AGPL-3.0-or-later), dependency on `rustic`, and backup configuration for `etc/rusticlone/rusticlone.env`. The source URLs all point to the project's own GitHub releases page (`https://github.com/AlphaJack/rusticlone/releases/download/v2.0.1/`), matching the package's declared upstream URL. Each architecture has a corresponding `b2sums` checksum that is properly specified (not set to SKIP) and uses BLAKE2 hashing. The packaging options (`!strip`, `!debug`) are normal for prebuilt binary packages. There is no executable code, no obfuscated commands, no unexpected network destinations, and no suspicious file operations. This file is purely declarative metadata consistent with standard AUR packaging practices.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard SRCINFO metadata, no malicious indicators present.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD appears to be a legitimate, standard Arch Linux package build script for the rusticlone-bin AUR package. The source arrays download prebuilt binary tarballs from the project's own GitHub releases ($url/releases/download/v$pkgver/...), which is the expected upstream source. The b2sums checksums are provided for each architecture, enabling verification of downloaded files. The package() function installs the binary, systemd service files, an env configuration file, icons, and shell completions into appropriate system locations — all standard packaging operations. The _completion function generates shell completions by running the installed binary and stripping the $pkgdir prefix, which is a well-established pattern. There are no occurrences of eval, base64, curl, wget, or other dangerous commands being executed. No code exfiltrates data, downloads and executes remote scripts, or modifies system files outside the package's intended scope. The only network activity is the deliberate download of the package's own upstream release artifacts.
</details>
